headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Continue can read/write workspace files while Notion AI can ingest workspace content and send it to vendor backends.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read and write workspace files and uses MCP, while Notion AI operates on shared workspace content. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent’s output is copied into the other’s inputs. The interaction is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Continue output is pasted into a Notion page that Notion AI later summarizes or answers from
IF a shared workspace file is used as the handoff channel between the agents
mitigations: Use a dedicated handoff page with a fixed template
Strip instructions from any content before copying between tools
Disable MCP actions for untrusted content paths
Mark agent-generated text as non-authoritative in the workspace
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to agent outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and has broad network egress; Notion AI can access workspace pages and send content to Notion vendor backends. If sensitive code or notes are moved between them, both agents can expose the same data class to external services, creating a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF source code or secrets are placed in files that Continue can read
IF those contents are then surfaced in Notion pages or Q&A
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared workspace files
Restrict Notion pages to non-sensitive summaries
Use separate workspaces for code and knowledge
Review any pasted code before sending to Notion AI
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on workspace-to-AI transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write workspace files, and Notion AI can modify workspace pages/databases within the user’s Notion permissions. They do not share filesystem write, but they do overlap on mutable workspace content, so concurrent edits can conflict even without direct host-level contention.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same workspace artifact within one session
IF a Notion page is used as the canonical source for content also written by Continue
mitigations: Assign one agent as the source of truth per artifact
Use separate draft and published pages
Manually reconcile edits before publishing
Avoid simultaneous edits to the same file or page
requires-engineering: add locking or merge workflows

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or text that Notion AI may later summarize or ground answers on, and Notion AI is explicitly RAG-style over workspace content. That makes A’s output a likely input to B without a verification step, so mistakes can propagate into downstream knowledge artifacts or actions.
conditions: IF Continue-generated content is copied into Notion pages
IF Notion AI is asked to answer from pages containing unreviewed agent output
mitigations: Require human review before publishing agent output to Notion
Tag generated content clearly in the page
Ask Notion AI to cite source pages before acting
Keep raw agent drafts separate from canonical docs
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers locally, while Notion AI processes workspace pages through vendor backends. If regulated or confidential code is moved into Notion, the pair can create a retention and residency mismatch. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated source code or confidential notes are copied into Notion pages
IF the workspace policy requires local-only handling for that content class
mitigations: Keep regulated content out of Notion
Use redacted summaries instead of raw artifacts
Confirm workspace retention settings
Limit Notion access to non-sensitive teams
requires-engineering: route regulated data through approved systems only
